rites.name: Karurnoth
rites.text: Karurnoth is the concept of the sworn oath as it is spoken before the Courts of Sallus, an idea that binds the speaker's word into the fabric of the doors between worlds. In the Age of Trials it was the principle that gave a judgment the weight to hold a door shut or open for a thousand years.

rites.name: Selleonanum
rites.text: Selleonanum is the concept of a sacred trial of flame, set down by the Courts of Sallus during the Holy Age when the temples first bound their orders to the doors between worlds. It names the bargain a candidate makes with the fire that tests their oath.

rites.name: Thevsiaseth
rites.text: Thevsiaseth is the concept of the Weave, the woven lattice the makers plant in Sallus during the Seeding, when quiet powers lie dormant beneath the surface of the world. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it is invoked as the hidden thread that binds every oath and sacred fire to the land.

rites.name: Lasus
rites.text: Lasus is the Ground of Radiant Stillness, a concept in the Sallus omniverse that the sages of the Sixth Age taught as the hidden substrate beneath every sun's light. Its presence is said to make a star's fire recognize itself, so that all shining things are understood as reflections of one undivided lamp. Lasus is held to be the origin from which the great solar powers of Sallus arise.

rites.name: Xaevseth
rites.text: Xaevseth is the concept of the Walled Age in Sallus, the belief that a standing wall keeps the dark out and that a people is defined by what it refuses to cross. Its orders raised holding walls, its churches taught the sealing of gates, and its first crossings were treated as sacrilege until a bold few proved the wall could be walked over.

rites.name: Crordath
rites.text: Crordath is the concept of the Walled Age in Sallus, the long span in which holding walls, orders, and first crossings shaped how the people of the world kept what they claimed. It is understood as the patience that binds a boundary and the courage that opens one, and its presence is felt most in the groves and young kingdoms of the first sovereign's time.

rites.name: Cisteorium
rites.text: Cisteorium is a crimson-hued alchemical principle of the Sallus cosmos, said to be the refining fire that turns the hungers of the heart into clarity and resolve. Its adepts describe it as a furious, sweet-burning current that consumes craving and leaves behind a steady light.

rites.name: Nones
rites.text: Nones is the Hollow Lantern of the Sallus pantheon, a concept-entity who keeps the threshold between waking and the unseen shore. Its light is said to be spent on every soul that crosses, yet never runs short.

rites.name: Liareolus
rites.text: Liareolus is a wrathful sovereign of inner light in the mythic age of Sallus, whose blazing gaze scours away the rot of greed and fear from those he watches over. His fire does not destroy the faithful but burns the clutter of the soul until a clear path opens toward awakening.

rites.name: Anakaeno
rites.text: Anakaeno is the concept of a branching ending, a single thread the Library of Sallus shelves among the futures that might yet come to pass. In the age of the first sovereign, when groves were still growing into kingdoms, it was said to be the quiet pressure that bent a harvest toward one outcome over another.

rites.name: Meravarum
rites.text: Meravarum is the concept of the Three Futures in Sallus, the principle by which the ending branches and every outcome is shelved in the Library. In the Holy Age, when temples and orders hold the sky's fires, it is invoked as the hand that decides which future is kept.

rites.name: Crodar
rites.text: Crodar is a concept in the Sallus cosmology, understood as the principle by which the Three Futures branch and the Library shelves each outcome for later reading. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, its presence was felt as a pressure of foreseen endings that priests tried to hold steady.
